summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Acquired immunity is divided into Humoral Immunity (B-cells producing circulating H2L2 antibodies against extracellular pathogens) and Cell-Mediated Immunity (T-cells defending against intracellular viruses, cancer, and driving graft/transplant rejection). Five antibody isotypes (IgG, IgA, IgM, IgE, IgD) perform specialized effector functions.

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 4.1 Humoral vs. Cell-Mediated Immunity
- **Humoral Immunity (Antibody-Mediated Immunity / AMI)**:
  - Driven by **B-Lymphocytes** (matured in bone marrow).
  - Upon antigen activation, B-cells proliferate into **Plasma Cells** (which secrete millions of soluble antibodies into blood plasma and lymph) and **Memory B-Cells**.
  - Protects against extracellular bacteria, viruses in circulation, and exotoxins.
- **Cell-Mediated Immunity (CMI)**:
  - Driven by **T-Lymphocytes** (matured in the **Thymus**).
  - Major Subsets: $\text{CD4}^+$ Helper T-cells ($T_H$) and $\text{CD8}^+$ Cytotoxic T-cells ($T_C$).
  - Fights intracellular pathogens (e.g., *Mycobacterium tuberculosis*, viruses inside host cells), cancer cells, and executes **Graft / Organ Transplant Rejection** (tissue matching and immunosuppressants like *Cyclosporin A* are required).

### 4.2 Antibody Structure ($\text{H}_2\text{L}_2$ Architecture)
- Y-shaped glycoprotein composed of **$2\text{ Heavy (H) chains}$** ($\approx 50\text{ kDa}$) and **$2\text{ Light (L) chains}$** ($\approx 25\text{ kDa}$) held together by inter-chain **Disulfide Bonds ($-\text{S}-\text{S}-$)**.
- **$F_{ab}$ Region**: Antigen-binding fragment located at the tips of the Y containing hypervariable regions ($V_H / V_L$) that form the paratope matching the epitope.
- **$F_c$ Region**: Crystallizable constant region ($C_H$) that binds host cell receptors (macrophages, mast cells) and activates complement.

### 4.3 Five Immunoglobulin Isotypes

| Isotype | Physical Structure | Serum Abundance | Primary Physiological & Clinical Roles |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **$\text{IgG}$** | Monomer ($\text{H}_2\text{L}_2$) | **$75\text{--}80\%$** (Most abundant) | Dominates secondary immune responses; **ONLY antibody that crosses the placenta** to protect fetus |
| **$\text{IgA}$** | Dimer with J-Chain | $10\text{--}15\%$ | Secretory antibody present in **Colostrum**, tears, saliva, and gut mucus; protects mucosal surfaces |
| **$\text{IgM}$** | Pentamer with J-Chain | $5\text{--}10\%$ | Largest antibody ($900\text{ kDa}$); first antibody class produced during primary immune response; potent agglutinator |
| **$\text{IgE}$** | Monomer ($\text{H}_2\text{L}_2$) | $<0.05\%$ (Trace) | Binds high-affinity $\text{Fc}\epsilon\text{RI}$ receptors on **Mast Cells & Basophils**; triggers **Allergies** & helminth defense |
| **$\text{IgD}$** | Monomer ($\text{H}_2\text{L}_2$) | $<1\%$ | Serves as antigen receptor on naive B-lymphocyte surface |

conceptBreakdown.heading: Primary vs Secondary Immune Response
conceptBreakdown.title: Primary vs Secondary Immune Response
conceptBreakdown.content: Primary immune response has a long lag phase, low antibody titers, and is dominated by IgM; Secondary (anamnestic) response upon re-exposure is rapid, heightened, dominated by high-affinity IgG, due to immunological memory.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Major Histocompatibility Complex (MHC/HLA)
conceptBreakdown.title: Major Histocompatibility Complex (MHC/HLA)
conceptBreakdown.content: MHC Class I molecules present endogenous antigens to CD8+ Cytotoxic T-cells, while MHC Class II molecules on antigen-presenting cells (dendritic cells, macrophages) present exogenous antigens to CD4+ Helper T-cells.
